four-copy build, taking the alignment from 64 to 16 removes 14 608 rows for
1 255 µs — **0.086 µs a row**, against the 0.137 µs a row §2.11's MMA-only
control put on a full tile. A short tile multiplies its rows against the
same slab unpack as a full one: two 64-column slabs a K-step, ~300 VALU
instructions a lane, each of which costs the matrix pipe a clock (§2.10),
so ~600 clocks beside the 544 clocks of a 16-row tile's sixteen MMAs where
a full tile's 64 MMAs are 2 176. The rows a short tile drops are cheaper
rows. It is also why the m4 rung's two-copy form loses so little to the
four-copy one (6 183 against 6 138): the 16-row tail it rounds to 32 was
never going to run at the pipe. The down mode unpacks one slab a step, so
its rows are dearer and its gain larger.

| 4096 (m4) | 10 815 / 10 994 → 10 281 / 10 224 | 9 469 / 9 497 → 8 144 / 8 112 | 24 578 / 24 765 → 22 728 / 22 610 |

7 972 → 6 821 at 4096; the block 6 091 → 5 777, 8 953 → 8 613, **14 441 →

### 2.11 The grouped MoE GEMM's K loop as a software pipeline: the up projection 1.68x at 2048 tokens, bit-identical — **done** ✅ (2026-09-29)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G5): the LLM's prefill spends a quarter of a
token in `llm_moe_gemm.comp`'s up mode, which runs at 22 TFLOP/s executed
(P12: 21.1 useful), ~45% of the matrix pipe at its clock. §2.2 blamed the
LDS round trip the quantised operand takes ("no extension exposes a
fragment's lane layout"); M11c's probe pinned that layout, so G5 was
written as "build the B fragments in registers". Before building it, the
kernel's parts were priced by their absence, the way G1 priced the DiT
GEMM's.

**Answer: the LDS round trip is not the cost; the per-step chain of
dependent, divergent bank loads is, and a pipeline that fetches a step
ahead and reads each block's bytes once takes the up projection from
11.5 to 6.8 ms a layer at 2048 tokens (1.68x), 2.01x at 512 and 1.57x at
4096, bit-identical.** G5's register-fragment idea was not built: with
both stagings removed the loop already runs at the matrix pipe's rate,
so there was nothing for it to buy, and at wave64 it would replicate the
unpack four times over.

**The kernel, from the disassembly** (`cmd/probe`, `RADV_DEBUG=asm`, the
shipped `up_q4k_m4`: one wave64 of a 4×4 tile grid, two 64-column slabs,
BK 32). One K-step is: four permutation loads, four gathered `uvec4` of
the block input into LDS; for each of the lane's two slab columns a
sixteen-byte block header, two `uvec4` of nibbles, ~150 VALU of scale
decode and affine, four `ds_store_b128`; then 96 `ds_load_b64` (24
fragments, 8 VGPRs each) and 64 MMAs. 256 VGPRs, no spill, four
subgroups a SIMD, and **no `s_barrier` at all** (one wave a workgroup;
the compiler drops it). Every load of the step is issued after the
previous step's MMAs and waited for before this step's, and each bank
load is 64 lanes at 64 different rows 1440 bytes apart: sixty-four cache
lines an instruction, of which each lane uses sixteen bytes, and the same
lines again on the next step (a header serves eight steps, a nibble group
two).

**The controls** (`-D` knobs on `llm_moe_gemm.comp`, never shipped, wrong
by construction; `cmd/llm -moe -tokens 2048 -iters 60`, layer 3, the 4k
trace's real routing, the m4 rung; each arm loaded through `LLM_MOE_SPV`;
100 ms clock and package samples, median 2450–2610 MHz at 115–131 W
across the arms, so the ratios stand):

| arm | `moe.up` µs | vs shipped | what it takes away |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| shipped `up_q4k_m4` (embedded and rebuilt: 11 527 / 11 542) | 11 530 | 1.00x | |
| `MOE_L0_A`: every gathered row from token zero | 10 532 | 1.09x | the A gather's fetch |
| `MOE_NO_ASTAGE`: no A staging | 10 477 | 1.10x | A's loads, VALU and stores |
| `MOE_L0_BANK=2`: the real 64 rows, the same bytes every step | 8 810 | **1.31x** | the bank's fetch, not its divergence |
| `MOE_NIB_ONLY`: `float16_t(nib)`, no header, scale or affine (P12-3) | 8 429 | 1.37x | the scale path |
| `MOE_L0_BANK=1`: every lane's bank bytes from one row | 8 015 | **1.44x** | the bank's fetch and its divergence |
| `MOE_L0_BANK=1` + `MOE_L0_A` | 7 368 | 1.57x | every fetch |
| `MOE_NO_UNPACK`: no B unpack (stale slabs) | 6 560 | **1.76x** | B's loads, VALU and stores |
| `MOE_NO_UNPACK` + `MOE_NO_ASTAGE`: the MMAs and fragment reads alone | 5 333 | 2.16x | both stagings |
| `MOE_FRAG2`: every fragment read twice (192 `ds_load_b64`) | 12 512 | 0.92x | (adds the LDS reads) |
| two wave64 waves of 2×4 tiles (same 64 rows) | 11 400 | 1.01x | |
| the same at wave32 | 11 386 | 1.01x | |

Three things. **The loop without its stagings runs at the pipe**: 255
GFLOP of executed MMAs in 5.33 ms is 47.8 TFLOP/s, against a ceiling of
47–50 at the 2450–2630 MHz the arm sampled — the 24 fragment reads a
step cost ~8% (`MOE_FRAG2` adds them again for 8.5%), and that is the
whole of the "LDS round trip". **The bank side is 30–43% of the step
and most of it is the fetch**: making the loads L0 hits with the same
divergence (`L0_BANK=2`) recovers 1.31x of the 1.44x, so the sixty-four
lines an instruction cost ~4 points and the re-reading of them across
steps and the latency in front of every step cost ~25. **The VALU is a
smaller share than P12 read it as**: the scale path is 1.37x when gutted,
but that arm also deletes the header loads.

**The arm: the K loop as a software pipeline** (`-DPIPE`, the Q4_K up
mode at BK 32). The bytes a lane will unpack at step k+1 — its `uvec4`
of the gathered rows and, per slab column, the block header and the
nibble group — are fetched into registers before step k's MMAs issue and
unpacked from registers at the top of the next trip; the permutation
entries, invariant across K, are read once before the loop. `PIPE=2`
adds the reuse the layout allows: **the header is fetched once per
256-element super-block and the nibble group once per two steps**, so a
super-block costs a lane 9 bank load instructions instead of 24. The
unpack, the LDS slabs and the fragment reads are the shipped ones, so the
result is bit-identical.

| build (m4 unless said; 60 iters; two runs where two numbers) | 512 tokens (m2) | 2048 | 4096 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| shipped | 6 508 / 6 518 | 11 512 / 11 533 | 17 106 / 17 243 |
| `PIPE=1`: a step ahead, every load every step | 6 185 / 6 199 (1.05x) | 11 054 / 11 127 (1.04x) | 15 008 / 15 090 (1.14x) |
| **`PIPE=2`: … and each block's bytes once** | **3 241 (2.01x)** | **6 837 (1.68x)** | **10 925 (1.57x)** |
| `PIPE=2` as two wave32 waves of 2×4 tiles | | 6 875 | |
| `PIPE=1` with two register sets (ping-pong) | 5 035 (m2) | 11 159 (two waves 2×4) / 12 073 (four waves 1×4) | 15 629 |

Executed rate at 2048: 22.1 → 37.3 TFLOP/s (useful, at the m4 rung's
1.90x padding: 11.7 → 19.6). At 512 the m2 rung's `moe.up` is now below
`moe.down`'s 3.0 ms for the first time.

**What the ladder inside the arm says.** `PIPE=1` alone is worth 4–14%:
the loads are in flight behind the MMAs, but the compiler still waits on
them inside the MMA block (`s_waitcnt vmcnt(5)`, `vmcnt(4)` between
`v_wmma`s) because the allocator lands them in temporaries and copies
them to the loop-carried registers there — ~110 `v_mov` a trip, §2.10's
move storm on a different kernel. A two-set form, so the fetch has no
live value to preserve, was built to remove the copies and **spills at
m4** (pre-schedule 359 VGPRs against 256) and buys nothing where it fits
(two-wave 2×4: 11 159; four-wave 1×4: 12 073; m2 at 512: 5 035 against
`PIPE=2`'s 3 241). What made the difference was `PIPE=2`'s reuse: 2.7x
fewer bank load instructions a super-block, none of them re-requesting
lines the L0 just dropped. That is the `L0_BANK=2` control's 1.31x, and
the pipeline then takes the latency on top of it, past the `L0_BANK=1`
arm (8 015) that still issued and waited on three loads a step.

**Register and spill line** (`RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats`, wave64, `PIPE=2`):
m1 216 VGPRs, m2 240, m4 256, w2m1 192, w4m1 96, n1m1 96, n2m1 144; no
spills, no scratch; m4 is 1544 instructions against the shipped 1473.

**Gates.** `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (every rung against m2/m2, `maxAbs
== 0`) on each pipelined geometry alone and the whole `TestMoEGPU*` suite
with all seven loaded at once: pass. The shipped `.spv` rebuilt from the
edited source with no knob is byte-for-byte the same instruction stream
(1473 instructions, 256 VGPRs; the SPIR-V differs in id numbering only).

**Refused on the way**: the register-built B fragment (G5 as written —
at wave64 a fragment is 4x replicated, so the unpack would run four
times for a round trip that costs 8%); a wave32 build of the m4 tile
(spills 217); the two-set pipeline (above).

**In the whole model** (`cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048,4096,8192 -ctx
8192`, 48 layers, `LLM_MOE_BANK`/`LLM_DENSE_BANK` at the shipped plans
with `LLM_BANK_CACHE`, the old and new binaries interleaved twice the same
hour): prefill **1194 / 1206 → 1407 / 1408 tok/s at 2048 tokens (1.17x)**,
1317 / 1339 → 1494 / 1495 at 4096 (1.13x), 1306 / 1345 → 1459 / 1462 at
8192 (1.10x). The share falls with the ubatch because the up projection's
padding factor falls with it (1.90x at 2048, 1.46x at 4096) and the rest
of the token does not move. The embedded builds pass the whole
`TestMoEGPU*` suite; the 1024-token ladder on them (m2 4 487 µs against
m4 4 600) keeps `moeGEMMPlanFor`'s m2/m4 boundary where it was.

**The down mode, measured, does not want it.** The same pipeline written
for the block-32 down formats (B only: its A operand is read straight
from the arena by the fragment loads; Q5_1 six words a step, Q4_1 five,
Q8_0 ten, IQ4_NL its nine-word pair once per two steps under `PIPE=2`),
every build spill-free and the whole `TestMoEGPU*` suite passing with all
twenty loaded:

| `moe.down`, µs a layer, m4 (m2 at 512) | 512 | 2048 | 4096 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q5_1 (the checkpoint's; layer 3) shipped | 2 995 / 2 982 | 6 587 / 6 582 | 9 507 |
| Q5_1 `PIPE=2` | 3 000 | 6 607 / 6 613 | 9 487 |
| IQ4_NL (the served format, `LLM_MOE_BANK=down_exps=iq4_nl`) shipped | 2 718 | 5 634 | 8 264 |
| **IQ4_NL `PIPE=2`** | **2 266 (1.20x)** | **5 366 (1.05x)** | **7 946 (1.04x)** |

Q5_1 moves by nothing, though its `L0_BANK` control read 1.29x — so what
that control removed was not latency the pipeline could hide but the
load's own cost, and a 32-element block a step has no reuse to hoist.
IQ4_NL gains exactly what its pair layout allows, the second half of the
pair read from a register instead of re-fetched. The IQ4_NL builds ship
with `PIPE=2` (whole-model prefill 1408 → 1422 tok/s at 2048 and 1502 →
1507 at 4096 on top of the up projection's gain, two runs each); Q5_1,
Q4_1 and Q8_0 keep the plain loop. The down mode's
remaining cost sits with its A fragment loads (sixteen `buffer_load_b128`
a step, issued inside the MMA block and not pipelined: a fragment cannot
be carried across the loop without §2.9's element-by-element copy).

**What is left.** The Q5_K up build (layer 2 of 48) keeps the plain loop.
The plan chooser (`moeGEMMPlanFor`) was re-measured on the pipelined
builds and its m2/m4 boundary stands (m2 4 487 µs against m4 4 600 at
1024 tokens). The executed rate at 2048 is now 37 TFLOP/s of a ~49
ceiling with a 1.90x padding factor on top: the next lever on the up
kernel is the padding, not the loop, and on the down kernel the A
fragment loads.

**Reproduce.** The shipped builds are the seven `llm_moe_up_q4k_*` and
the five `llm_moe_down_iq4nl_*` generate lines in `shaders/shaders.go`
with `-DPIPE=2`. The controls are
`-DMOE_NO_UNPACK=1`, `-DMOE_NO_ASTAGE=1`, `-DMOE_NIB_ONLY=1`,
`-DMOE_L0_BANK=1|2`, `-DMOE_L0_A=1`, `-DMOE_FRAG2=1`, `-DWAVE=32` on
`llm_moe_gemm.comp`, compiled to the scratchpad and loaded with
`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=path.spv` (comma-separated for several,
`LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32` for a wave32 build) into `cmd/llm -moe` or the
`llm` tests, which take the same override. The clock beside it: a 100 ms
loop over `hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average`; a `-moe` arm is
about two seconds of device time, so quote the median of the samples
above 100 W.

many of a block's rows are real, and the single-wave builds of
`llm_moe_gemm.comp` are `SHORT` builds that run one of WM copies of their
K loop and store chosen by a uniform switch on that count — no bound inside
the unrolled loops, the same MMAs per real row in the same order, so it is
**bit-identical** to the padded schedule (`TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` at
`maxAbs == 0` across every mixed plan, `TestGraphLogits`'s whole-model
diagnostics reproduced to the digit against the old build). At 2048
tokens `moe.up` **6 994 / 7 029 → 6 314 / 6 255 µs a layer (1.11x)**,
`moe.down` **6 577 / 6 609 → 5 370 / 5 339 (1.23x)** on the checkpoint's
Q5_1 and **5 373 → 4 209 (1.28x)** on the served IQ4_NL, the block
**1.13–1.14x**; whole-model prefill **1 417 / 1 419 → 1 514 / 1 513 tok/s
at 2048 (1.07x)**, 1 500 / 1 502 → 1 549 / 1 543 at 4096, 1 461 / 1 467 →
1 481 / 1 483 at 8192. And with the padding no longer a price on the wide
rung, the plan's m2/m4 boundary moves from 1024 tokens to 256.

**What the padding was.** `Schedule()` on the 4k trace's real routing,
executed rows over real (the tile count is the same at both alignments,
because an expert's last block is still a block):

| tokens | rows | pad 64 (was) | pad 16 | pad 32 (what the up m4 build executes) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 5 120 | 11 904 (2.33x) | 8 064 (1.57x) | 11 904 at the m2 rung's own 32 |
| 1024 | 10 240 | 17 536 (1.71x, m2) | 13 472 (1.32x) | 17 536 |
| 2048 | 20 480 | 38 912 (1.90x) | 24 304 (1.19x) | 28 832 (1.41x) |
| 4096 | 40 960 | 59 904 (1.46x) | 44 816 (1.09x) | 49 536 (1.21x) |

**The arm.** The record's third word has carried the block's real rows
since C5 (the decode GEMV skips its padding with it); the GEMM never read
it. A SHORT build rounds it up to the schedule's alignment (`pc.gemmM`,
`MoEGPU.pad`, so a plan that mixes in a multi-wave rung and aligns to 64
still runs whole blocks) and takes `wmEff = ceil(rows / 16)`; the K loop
and the epilogue are macros over the tile count and the kernel holds one
instantiation per height behind `switch (wmEff)`. The pipeline's first
fetch, the permutation entries and the accumulators' zeroing sit before
the switch and are shared. MODE 0's A staging still fills all 64 rows —
the loads are in flight behind the MMAs, and the rows past the block are
valid entries of the permuted space (the permutation sentinel-fills to a
whole 64-row block past its end, which `maxRows` has room for) — so only
the MMAs and the stores of the missing tiles go. `llm_moe_perm.comp` cuts
`ceil(padded / bm)` records an expert instead of `padded / bm`; the
host's `pad()` is the max over the plan's rungs of `moeAlign` (16 for a
single-wave rung or a GEMV, the block for `w2m1`/`w4m1`), `maxTiles` has a
pad-below-block form, the tile arenas are sized for the widest alignment
whatever the plan, and the shared expert's host-written list gets a short
last block the same way. `LLM_MOE_PAD=16|32|64` forces the alignment for a
screen.

**The register and code line** (`cmd/probe`, `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats`,
wave64), which decided the form the up build ships in:

| build | copies | VGPRs | spilled | instructions | code |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `up_q4k_m4` shipped (§2.11) | — | 256 | 0 | 1 544 | 8.6 KB |
| SHORT, every height | 1, 2, 3, 4 | 256 | **15** | 4 524 | 25.6 KB |
| SHORT without the 3-tile copy | 1, 2, 4 | 256 | **15** | 3 339 | 18.9 KB |
| SHORT without the 1-tile copy | 2, 3, 4 | 256 | **15** | 3 753 | 21.2 KB |
| **SHORT, `SHORT_STEP=2` (shipped)** | **2, 4** | 256 | **0** | 2 504 | 14.1 KB |
| `up_q4k_m2` SHORT | 1, 2 | 240 | 0 | 1 732 | |
| `up_q5k_m4` / `up_q80_m4` SHORT (plain loop) | 1–4 | 256 | 0 | 5 979 / 4 811 | |
| `down_q51_m4` / `q80` / `q41` SHORT | 1–4 | 120 | 0 | 1 893 / 1 961 / 1 601 | |
| `down_iq4nl_m4` SHORT (`PIPE=2`) | 1–4 | 144 | 0 | 2 448 | |

Any third copy of the Q4_K up loop spills eleven to fifteen registers
that its epilogue needs across the K loop (the scratch stores sit before
the first copy's loop, the reloads among its sigmoid), and a control run
of the four-copy build with the alignment forced to 64 — every block
whole, every workgroup in the 4-tile copy — is **9% slower than the
shipped kernel on the same work** (7 393 against 6 798 µs), which is the
spill and the code. The two-copy form costs nothing on full blocks and
rounds a 16-row tail up to 32 rows of MMA; **its store is still bounded by
the real count**, because the rows past the block are the next expert's,
and the first cut that stored the rounded tiles was a race the ladder test
caught at once. So the up m4 build executes rows as at an alignment of
32, and the down builds, with their 120–144 registers, keep all four
copies and execute exactly the alignment-16 rows.

**The screen** (`LLM_MOE_SPV` on `cmd/llm -moe -tokens 512,1024,2048,4096
-iters 60`, layer 3, the real routing, Q5_1 down; 100 ms clock and package
samples, median 2 700–2 850 MHz at 146–149 W across the arms):

| 2048 tokens, µs a layer | rows | `moe.up` | `moe.down` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| shipped (§2.11) | 1.90x | 6 798 | 6 589 |
| SHORT four copies, `LLM_MOE_PAD=64` (the control) | 1.90x | 7 393 | 6 553 |
| SHORT four copies, alignment 16 | 1.19x | 6 138 | 5 345 |
| SHORT two copies, alignment 32 | 1.41x | 6 183 | 5 691 |

**Why the up projection keeps less than the rows it sheds.** On the same
four-copy build, taking the alignment from 64 to 16 removes 14 608 rows for
1 255 µs — **0.086 µs a row**, against the 0.137 µs a row §2.11's MMA-only
control put on a full tile. A short tile multiplies its rows against the
same slab unpack as a full one: two 64-column slabs a K-step, ~300 VALU
instructions a lane, each of which costs the matrix pipe a clock (§2.10),
so ~600 clocks beside the 544 clocks of a 16-row tile's sixteen MMAs where
a full tile's 64 MMAs are 2 176. The rows a short tile drops are cheaper
rows. It is also why the m4 rung's two-copy form loses so little to the
four-copy one (6 183 against 6 138): the 16-row tail it rounds to 32 was
never going to run at the pipe. The down mode unpacks one slab a step, so
its rows are dearer and its gain larger.

**The shipped builds, old and new binaries interleaved twice the same
hour** (`cmd/llm -moe`, the plan as it was, µs a layer):

| tokens (rung) | `moe.up` old → new | `moe.down` (Q5_1) old → new | block old → new |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 (m2) | 3 139 / 3 192 → 3 070 / 3 066 | 3 013 / 2 991 → 2 768 / 2 749 | 6 805 / 6 833 → 6 488 / 6 464 |
| 1024 (m2) | 4 463 / 4 479 → 4 438 / 4 382 | 3 929 / 3 934 → 3 676 / 3 685 | 9 643 / 9 671 → 9 366 / 9 311 |
| **2048 (m4)** | **6 994 / 7 029 → 6 314 / 6 255** | **6 577 / 6 609 → 5 370 / 5 339** | **15 733 / 15 793 → 13 822 / 13 721** |
| 4096 (m4) | 10 815 / 10 994 → 10 281 / 10 224 | 9 469 / 9 497 → 8 144 / 8 112 | 24 578 / 24 765 → 22 728 / 22 610 |

With the served down format (`LLM_MOE_BANK=down_exps=iq4_nl`): `moe.down`
2 265 → 2 037 at 512, 3 202 → 2 978 at 1024, **5 373 → 4 209 at 2048**,
7 972 → 6 821 at 4096; the block 6 091 → 5 777, 8 953 → 8 613, **14 441 →
12 727**, 23 264 → 21 471.

**The plan.** The rung ladder on the SHORT builds (`-ladder -iters 30`,
block µs, `m2/m2` against `m4/m4`): 3 075 / 3 126 at 64 tokens, 3 822 /
3 869 at 128, 4 737 / 4 735 at 256, **6 460 / 6 380 at 512, 9 361 / 8 999
at 1024** — the wide rung no longer pays for its width in rows, only in
the tail its two copies round up, so `moeGEMMPlanFor` switches to m4 above
256 tokens instead of above 1024. The mixed pairs are within 1% of the
diagonal at every count; the multi-wave rungs, still aligned to their
block, lose 1.2–1.6x at every count and stay out of the plan. On the plan
as shipped (`results/g5c_moe_short_r{1,2}.csv`, 60 iters, two runs) the
block is **6 312 / 6 313 µs at 512 tokens** against the old schedule's
6 805 / 6 833 (1.08x) and **8 800 / 8 810 at 1024** against 9 643 / 9 671
(1.10x), 13 876 / 13 767 at 2048, 22 615 / 22 703 at 4096; with the
served IQ4_NL down 5 508, 7 879 / 7 870, 12 628 / 12 633 and 21 420 /
21 371.

**In the whole model** (`cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048,4096,8192 -ctx 8192`,
48 layers, the shipped banks under `LLM_BANK_CACHE`, old and new binaries
interleaved twice): **1 416.5 / 1 418.6 → 1 514.0 / 1 513.2 tok/s at 2048
(1.07x)**, 1 499.7 / 1 502.1 → 1 549.4 / 1 542.8 at 4096 (1.03x), 1 461.4 /
1 466.7 → 1 480.8 / 1 482.7 at 8192 (1.01x); the share falls with the
ubatch as the padding factor did. `TestGraphLogits` on the new test binary
prints the same `result_output` line to the digit as on the old one
(`maxAbs 1.987e+00 at 19208, rms 3.314e-01`, argmax 11751 against 561,
0.4920 apart).

**What is left on this kernel.** The short tiles are bound by the slab
unpack, which is now the largest term in the up projection at every rung:
~300 VALU a lane a K-step for two slabs, every instruction a matrix clock.
That is G5's remaining argument for `v_perm`/`v_cvt_pk` sequences over
per-element work (P12-3 priced the scale path at 1.37x when gutted, header
loads included), and it would lift the short tiles most. The down mode's A
fragment loads inside its MMA block (§2.11) are the other.

**Reproduce.** The 27 single-wave `llm_moe_*` generate lines in
`shaders/shaders.go` carry `-DSHORT=1`, the Q4_K up m4 line
`-DSHORT_STEP=2`. `LLM_MOE_PAD=64` with the SHORT builds is the
whole-block control; a pre-§2.12 build loaded through `LLM_MOE_SPV` needs
it or it writes the next expert's rows. The runs above are
`results/g5c_moe_short_r{1,2}.csv` (Q5_1 down) and
`results/g5c_moe_short_iq4nl_r{1,2}.csv` (the served format), on the plan
as shipped.

[← IDEAS.md](ideas.md) · [research index](README.md) · the grouped MoE GEMM's K loop

### 2.11 The grouped MoE GEMM's K loop as a software pipeline: the up projection 1.68x at 2048 tokens, bit-identical — **done** ✅ (2026-09-29)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G5): the LLM's prefill spends a quarter of a
token in `llm_moe_gemm.comp`'s up mode, which runs at 22 TFLOP/s executed
(P12: 21.1 useful), ~45% of the matrix pipe at its clock. §2.2 blamed the
LDS round trip the quantised operand takes ("no extension exposes a
fragment's lane layout"); M11c's probe pinned that layout, so G5 was
written as "build the B fragments in registers". Before building it, the
kernel's parts were priced by their absence, the way G1 priced the DiT
GEMM's.

**Answer: the LDS round trip is not the cost; the per-step chain of
dependent, divergent bank loads is, and a pipeline that fetches a step
ahead and reads each block's bytes once takes the up projection from
11.5 to 6.8 ms a layer at 2048 tokens (1.68x), 2.01x at 512 and 1.57x at
4096, bit-identical.** G5's register-fragment idea was not built: with
both stagings removed the loop already runs at the matrix pipe's rate,
so there was nothing for it to buy, and at wave64 it would replicate the
unpack four times over.

**The kernel, from the disassembly** (`cmd/probe`, `RADV_DEBUG=asm`, the
shipped `up_q4k_m4`: one wave64 of a 4×4 tile grid, two 64-column slabs,
BK 32). One K-step is: four permutation loads, four gathered `uvec4` of
the block input into LDS; for each of the lane's two slab columns a
sixteen-byte block header, two `uvec4` of nibbles, ~150 VALU of scale
decode and affine, four `ds_store_b128`; then 96 `ds_load_b64` (24
fragments, 8 VGPRs each) and 64 MMAs. 256 VGPRs, no spill, four
subgroups a SIMD, and **no `s_barrier` at all** (one wave a workgroup;
the compiler drops it). Every load of the step is issued after the
previous step's MMAs and waited for before this step's, and each bank
load is 64 lanes at 64 different rows 1440 bytes apart: sixty-four cache
lines an instruction, of which each lane uses sixteen bytes, and the same
lines again on the next step (a header serves eight steps, a nibble group
two).

**The controls** (`-D` knobs on `llm_moe_gemm.comp`, never shipped, wrong
by construction; `cmd/llm -moe -tokens 2048 -iters 60`, layer 3, the 4k
trace's real routing, the m4 rung; each arm loaded through `LLM_MOE_SPV`;
100 ms clock and package samples, median 2450–2610 MHz at 115–131 W
across the arms, so the ratios stand):

| arm | `moe.up` µs | vs shipped | what it takes away |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| shipped `up_q4k_m4` (embedded and rebuilt: 11 527 / 11 542) | 11 530 | 1.00x | |
| `MOE_L0_A`: every gathered row from token zero | 10 532 | 1.09x | the A gather's fetch |
| `MOE_NO_ASTAGE`: no A staging | 10 477 | 1.10x | A's loads, VALU and stores |
| `MOE_L0_BANK=2`: the real 64 rows, the same bytes every step | 8 810 | **1.31x** | the bank's fetch, not its divergence |
| `MOE_NIB_ONLY`: `float16_t(nib)`, no header, scale or affine (P12-3) | 8 429 | 1.37x | the scale path |
| `MOE_L0_BANK=1`: every lane's bank bytes from one row | 8 015 | **1.44x** | the bank's fetch and its divergence |
| `MOE_L0_BANK=1` + `MOE_L0_A` | 7 368 | 1.57x | every fetch |
| `MOE_NO_UNPACK`: no B unpack (stale slabs) | 6 560 | **1.76x** | B's loads, VALU and stores |
| `MOE_NO_UNPACK` + `MOE_NO_ASTAGE`: the MMAs and fragment reads alone | 5 333 | 2.16x | both stagings |
| `MOE_FRAG2`: every fragment read twice (192 `ds_load_b64`) | 12 512 | 0.92x | (adds the LDS reads) |
| two wave64 waves of 2×4 tiles (same 64 rows) | 11 400 | 1.01x | |
| the same at wave32 | 11 386 | 1.01x | |

Three things. **The loop without its stagings runs at the pipe**: 255
GFLOP of executed MMAs in 5.33 ms is 47.8 TFLOP/s, against a ceiling of
47–50 at the 2450–2630 MHz the arm sampled — the 24 fragment reads a
step cost ~8% (`MOE_FRAG2` adds them again for 8.5%), and that is the
whole of the "LDS round trip". **The bank side is 30–43% of the step
and most of it is the fetch**: making the loads L0 hits with the same
divergence (`L0_BANK=2`) recovers 1.31x of the 1.44x, so the sixty-four
lines an instruction cost ~4 points and the re-reading of them across
steps and the latency in front of every step cost ~25. **The VALU is a
smaller share than P12 read it as**: the scale path is 1.37x when gutted,
but that arm also deletes the header loads.

**The arm: the K loop as a software pipeline** (`-DPIPE`, the Q4_K up
mode at BK 32). The bytes a lane will unpack at step k+1 — its `uvec4`
of the gathered rows and, per slab column, the block header and the
nibble group — are fetched into registers before step k's MMAs issue and
unpacked from registers at the top of the next trip; the permutation
entries, invariant across K, are read once before the loop. `PIPE=2`
adds the reuse the layout allows: **the header is fetched once per
256-element super-block and the nibble group once per two steps**, so a
super-block costs a lane 9 bank load instructions instead of 24. The
unpack, the LDS slabs and the fragment reads are the shipped ones, so the
result is bit-identical.

| build (m4 unless said; 60 iters; two runs where two numbers) | 512 tokens (m2) | 2048 | 4096 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| shipped | 6 508 / 6 518 | 11 512 / 11 533 | 17 106 / 17 243 |
| `PIPE=1`: a step ahead, every load every step | 6 185 / 6 199 (1.05x) | 11 054 / 11 127 (1.04x) | 15 008 / 15 090 (1.14x) |
| **`PIPE=2`: … and each block's bytes once** | **3 241 (2.01x)** | **6 837 (1.68x)** | **10 925 (1.57x)** |
| `PIPE=2` as two wave32 waves of 2×4 tiles | | 6 875 | |
| `PIPE=1` with two register sets (ping-pong) | 5 035 (m2) | 11 159 (two waves 2×4) / 12 073 (four waves 1×4) | 15 629 |

Executed rate at 2048: 22.1 → 37.3 TFLOP/s (useful, at the m4 rung's
1.90x padding: 11.7 → 19.6). At 512 the m2 rung's `moe.up` is now below
`moe.down`'s 3.0 ms for the first time.

**What the ladder inside the arm says.** `PIPE=1` alone is worth 4–14%:
the loads are in flight behind the MMAs, but the compiler still waits on
them inside the MMA block (`s_waitcnt vmcnt(5)`, `vmcnt(4)` between
`v_wmma`s) because the allocator lands them in temporaries and copies
them to the loop-carried registers there — ~110 `v_mov` a trip, §2.10's
move storm on a different kernel. A two-set form, so the fetch has no
live value to preserve, was built to remove the copies and **spills at
m4** (pre-schedule 359 VGPRs against 256) and buys nothing where it fits
(two-wave 2×4: 11 159; four-wave 1×4: 12 073; m2 at 512: 5 035 against
`PIPE=2`'s 3 241). What made the difference was `PIPE=2`'s reuse: 2.7x
fewer bank load instructions a super-block, none of them re-requesting
lines the L0 just dropped. That is the `L0_BANK=2` control's 1.31x, and
the pipeline then takes the latency on top of it, past the `L0_BANK=1`
arm (8 015) that still issued and waited on three loads a step.

**Register and spill line** (`RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats`, wave64, `PIPE=2`):
m1 216 VGPRs, m2 240, m4 256, w2m1 192, w4m1 96, n1m1 96, n2m1 144; no
spills, no scratch; m4 is 1544 instructions against the shipped 1473.

**Gates.** `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` (every rung against m2/m2, `maxAbs
== 0`) on each pipelined geometry alone and the whole `TestMoEGPU*` suite
with all seven loaded at once: pass. The shipped `.spv` rebuilt from the
edited source with no knob is byte-for-byte the same instruction stream
(1473 instructions, 256 VGPRs; the SPIR-V differs in id numbering only).

**Refused on the way**: the register-built B fragment (G5 as written —
at wave64 a fragment is 4x replicated, so the unpack would run four
times for a round trip that costs 8%); a wave32 build of the m4 tile
(spills 217); the two-set pipeline (above).

**In the whole model** (`cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048,4096,8192 -ctx
8192`, 48 layers, `LLM_MOE_BANK`/`LLM_DENSE_BANK` at the shipped plans
with `LLM_BANK_CACHE`, the old and new binaries interleaved twice the same
hour): prefill **1194 / 1206 → 1407 / 1408 tok/s at 2048 tokens (1.17x)**,
1317 / 1339 → 1494 / 1495 at 4096 (1.13x), 1306 / 1345 → 1459 / 1462 at
8192 (1.10x). The share falls with the ubatch because the up projection's
padding factor falls with it (1.90x at 2048, 1.46x at 4096) and the rest
of the token does not move. The embedded builds pass the whole
`TestMoEGPU*` suite; the 1024-token ladder on them (m2 4 487 µs against
m4 4 600) keeps `moeGEMMPlanFor`'s m2/m4 boundary where it was.

**The down mode, measured, does not want it.** The same pipeline written
for the block-32 down formats (B only: its A operand is read straight
from the arena by the fragment loads; Q5_1 six words a step, Q4_1 five,
Q8_0 ten, IQ4_NL its nine-word pair once per two steps under `PIPE=2`),
every build spill-free and the whole `TestMoEGPU*` suite passing with all
twenty loaded:

| `moe.down`, µs a layer, m4 (m2 at 512) | 512 | 2048 | 4096 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q5_1 (the checkpoint's; layer 3) shipped | 2 995 / 2 982 | 6 587 / 6 582 | 9 507 |
| Q5_1 `PIPE=2` | 3 000 | 6 607 / 6 613 | 9 487 |
| IQ4_NL (the served format, `LLM_MOE_BANK=down_exps=iq4_nl`) shipped | 2 718 | 5 634 | 8 264 |
| **IQ4_NL `PIPE=2`** | **2 266 (1.20x)** | **5 366 (1.05x)** | **7 946 (1.04x)** |

Q5_1 moves by nothing, though its `L0_BANK` control read 1.29x — so what
that control removed was not latency the pipeline could hide but the
load's own cost, and a 32-element block a step has no reuse to hoist.
IQ4_NL gains exactly what its pair layout allows, the second half of the
pair read from a register instead of re-fetched. The IQ4_NL builds ship
with `PIPE=2` (whole-model prefill 1408 → 1422 tok/s at 2048 and 1502 →
1507 at 4096 on top of the up projection's gain, two runs each); Q5_1,
Q4_1 and Q8_0 keep the plain loop. The down mode's
remaining cost sits with its A fragment loads (sixteen `buffer_load_b128`
a step, issued inside the MMA block and not pipelined: a fragment cannot
be carried across the loop without §2.9's element-by-element copy).

**What is left.** The Q5_K up build (layer 2 of 48) keeps the plain loop.
The plan chooser (`moeGEMMPlanFor`) was re-measured on the pipelined
builds and its m2/m4 boundary stands (m2 4 487 µs against m4 4 600 at
1024 tokens). The executed rate at 2048 is now 37 TFLOP/s of a ~49
ceiling with a 1.90x padding factor on top: the next lever on the up
kernel is the padding, not the loop, and on the down kernel the A
fragment loads.

**Reproduce.** The shipped builds are the seven `llm_moe_up_q4k_*` and
the five `llm_moe_down_iq4nl_*` generate lines in `shaders/shaders.go`
with `-DPIPE=2`. The controls are
`-DMOE_NO_UNPACK=1`, `-DMOE_NO_ASTAGE=1`, `-DMOE_NIB_ONLY=1`,
`-DMOE_L0_BANK=1|2`, `-DMOE_L0_A=1`, `-DMOE_FRAG2=1`, `-DWAVE=32` on
`llm_moe_gemm.comp`, compiled to the scratchpad and loaded with
`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=path.spv` (comma-separated for several,
`LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32` for a wave32 build) into `cmd/llm -moe` or the
`llm` tests, which take the same override. The clock beside it: a 100 ms
loop over `hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average`; a `-moe` arm is
about two seconds of device time, so quote the median of the samples
above 100 W.

description: "How to screen a build of the LLM's grouped MoE GEMM (llm_moe_gemm.comp) from disk, and the three traps hit doing it (2026-09-29/30)."

`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=/path/x.spv[,down_q51_m4=…]` (plus `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32`
for a wave32 build) loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk in place of the
embedded one, on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the `llm` tests. The rung names are
`moeSPIRV`'s keys in `llm/gpu_moe.go`; the auto plan is m2 at ≤256 tokens and
m4 above (moved from 1024 by §2.12), so a 2048-token screen must override
`up_q4k_m4` with a BM-64 build (WM×WAVES×16 = 64), not an m2-shaped one. The
shared expert runs the **Q8_0** builds of the same rungs (`up_q80_m4`,
`down_q80_m4`), so a screen that changes the schedule must load those too.

**Why:** three traps cost time (KERNELS.md G5a/G5c, research/2.11, 2.12).
The `llm` test binary looks for the checkpoint at `../models/…`, so run it
from `llm/` or every GPU test silently SKIPs and prints PASS. A `-moe` arm at
60 iters is ~2 s of device time, so the 100 ms clock sampler gets ~20 busy
samples an arm: quote the median of samples above 100 W, not the mean. And

name: valu-costs-matrix-clocks
description: On this RDNA3.5 part every VALU instruction beside a WMMA costs the matrix pipe ~1 clock (~3% per instruction per MMA at wave32); the shipped LDS GEMM lost 7% to register-allocator moves; how to price a kernel's non-MMA work with the issue probe.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Measured 2026-09-29 (KERNELS.md G-o8, research §2.10) with `shaders/wmma_issue_probe.comp` run through `PEAK_SPV=... PEAK_MMAS=16 PEAK_SUBGROUPS=8 PEAK_WAVE=32 go run ./cmd/bench peak`: the WMMA runs on the SIMD's VALU, so 4 independent fp32 FMAs per MMA cost 12%, 8 cost 20%, linearly (a wave32 MMA is ~34 clocks). LDS fragment reads at the GEMM's ratio cost only 3%, a barrier alone 0, the two together 9% (the post-barrier burst). The shipped `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` carried ~40 `v_swap`/`v_mov` a tile (RA assembling the second K tile's fragments while hoisted staging loads held registers); keeping the K tiles as a `[[dont_unroll]]` loop (`KT_LOOP`) plus non-`readonly` staging views (`STAGE_RW`, with a never-taken store so `nir_opt_access` cannot re-infer readonly and sink the loads) removed them: 80 → 85% per clock, bit-identical.

**Why:** every earlier GEMM lever counted bytes; nobody counted VALU issue, and it was the largest remaining term. `subgroupShuffleXor(v,16)` at wave32 is `v_permlanex16` (VALU, no LDS), so an exchange that halves LDS bytes still loses (−5%).

**How to apply:** before timing any coopmat kernel build, `RADV_DEBUG=asm go run ./cmd/probe x.spv 32` and count `v_swap|v_mov|v_cndmask|v_perm` per `v_wmma`; the budget is a few per MMA. Prefer a loop the compiler cannot reschedule over an unrolled body. Dequant (G5) and attention (G4) arms are priced by the same rule. See [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]], [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].

name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
description: "`go run` rebuilds per arm, and a rebuilt shared test binary is picked up by a still-running loop: build once per sweep under its own name, check ps before a second GPU run."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with

    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found

~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
until the end.

[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the
tree holds *then*, not what it held at launch. Even an edit that compiles
would silently measure a different binary in later arms, which is worse than
a crash.

**How to apply:** make the benchmark script `go build -o <scratchpad>/bench
./cmd/llm` **once at the top** and run that binary for every arm. Then the
tree is free to edit while it runs, and every arm is provably the same build.
Select arms with environment variables read at dispatch time (this is what
`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS` are for), never by rebuilding.

**2026-09-29, the same trap one level down.** A backgrounded swizzle sweep
ran `<scratchpad>/dit.test` once per arm; I then `go test -c -o` the *same
path* for the next experiment and launched it. Two GPU runs overlapped (each
timing the other's contention) and the old loop's later arms ran the new
binary. A shell `until grep -c ...` waiter hid it: the arms I waited on were
not the ones I thought. **Give every sweep its own binary name** (e.g.
`dit_swz.test`), and before starting a GPU run, check `ps` for another
`*.test` / `cmd/*` still on the device, or wait on the sweep's PID
([[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]).

---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
====
// moeSPVOverride is `LLM_MOE_SPV` (KERNELS.md G5): a build of the grouped
// GEMM loaded from disk in place of the embedded one, `up_q4k_m4=path.spv`,
// comma-separated, with `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE` the wave those builds were
// compiled for (64 unless said). It is this kernel's `H3_GEMM_SPV`: a
// screening knob for the ladder and the record, never the served path, and a
// build that is wrong by construction is still timed.
func moeSPVOverride() (map[string][]byte, uint32, error) {
	spec := os.Getenv("LLM_MOE_SPV")
	wave := uint32(moeWave)
	if spec == "" {
		return nil, wave, nil
	}
	out := map[string][]byte{}
	for _, kv := range strings.Split(spec, ",") {
		name, path, ok := strings.Cut(kv, "=")
		if !ok {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV entry %q is not name=path", kv)
		}
		if _, known := moeSPIRV[name]; !known {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV names %q, which is not a grouped GEMM build", name)
		}
		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV %s: %w", name, err)
		}
		out[name] = b
	}
	if w := os.Getenv("LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE"); w != "" {
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(w)
		if err != nil || (n != 32 && n != 64) {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE %q: want 32 or 64", w)
		}
		wave = uint32(n)
	}
	return out, wave, nil
}

func (g *MoEGPU) pipeline(name string, spirv []byte, spec vk.PipelineSpec) error {
	mod, err := g.dev.NewShaderModule(spirv)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("llm: shader moe.%s: %w", name, err)
	}
	g.mods = append(g.mods, mod)
	pipe, err := g.dev.NewPipeline(mod, spec)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("llm: pipeline moe.%s: %w", name, err)
	}

// moeSPVOverride is `LLM_MOE_SPV` (KERNELS.md G5): a build of the grouped
// GEMM loaded from disk in place of the embedded one, `up_q4k_m4=path.spv`,
// comma-separated, with `LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE` the wave those builds were
// compiled for (64 unless said). It is this kernel's `H3_GEMM_SPV`: a
// screening knob for the ladder and the record, never the served path, and a
// build that is wrong by construction is still timed.
func moeSPVOverride() (map[string][]byte, uint32, error) {
	spec := os.Getenv("LLM_MOE_SPV")
	wave := uint32(moeWave)
	if spec == "" {
		return nil, wave, nil
	}
	out := map[string][]byte{}
	for _, kv := range strings.Split(spec, ",") {
		name, path, ok := strings.Cut(kv, "=")
		if !ok {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV entry %q is not name=path", kv)
		}
		if _, known := moeSPIRV[name]; !known {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV names %q, which is not a grouped GEMM build", name)
		}
		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV %s: %w", name, err)
		}
		out[name] = b
	}
	if w := os.Getenv("LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE"); w != "" {
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(w)
		if err != nil || (n != 32 && n != 64) {
			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("llm: LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE %q: want 32 or 64", w)
		}
		wave = uint32(n)
	}
	return out, wave, nil
}

	mod, err := g.dev.NewShaderModule(spirv)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("llm: shader moe.%s: %w", name, err)
	}
	g.mods = append(g.mods, mod)
	pipe, err := g.dev.NewPipeline(mod, spec)
	if err != nil {

import re
p='shaders/llm_moe_gemm.comp'
s=open(p).read()

# 1. the knob, after MOE_FRAG2's default
old="""#ifndef MOE_FRAG2
#define MOE_FRAG2 0
#endif
"""
new="""#ifndef MOE_FRAG2
#define MOE_FRAG2 0
#endif
// NIB_F16 (KERNELS.md G5d): the Q4_K nibble read as an f16 *denormal*. The
// shipped unpack spends a `v_bfe_u32` and a `v_cvt_f32_u32` in front of every
// element's `v_fma_mixlo_f16`, and every VALU instruction costs the matrix
// pipe a clock (§2.10). A halfword whose low nibble is the value and whose
// other twelve bits are zero *is* the half `nib * 2^-24` — a denormal, exact —
// and `v_fma_mix` reads a half from either half of a word for free (op_sel).
// So a word's four nibbles become two masked words (`w & 0x000F000F` holds
// elements 0 and 2, `(w >> 8) & mask` elements 1 and 3): three instructions
// for four elements instead of eight, and the scale carries the 2^24 (2^20
// for the high nibble, whose halfword is `nib * 16`). `d * sc` is an
// 11-by-6-bit product, exact in fp32, and a power of two keeps it exact, so
// the fma sees the same operands to the bit and the slab is byte-identical
// (the ladder gate against a build without it says so). fp16 denormals are
// preserved by default under RADV; a build that flushed them would fail
// that gate at once, with every value `-dm`.
#ifndef NIB_F16
#define NIB_F16 0
#endif
// MOE_KT_LOOP keeps the MMA block's two K tiles as a loop the compiler
// cannot unroll, §2.10's `KT_LOOP` on this kernel: the unrolled block carries
// ~50 `v_mov`/`v_swap` a step from the allocator at 256 VGPRs.
#ifndef MOE_KT_LOOP
#define MOE_KT_LOOP 0
#endif
#if MOE_KT_LOOP
#define KT_UNROLL [[dont_unroll]]
#else
#define KT_UNROLL [[unroll]]
#endif
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)

# 2. the plain Q4_K body
old="""    uint sh = sub * 4u;                                                                         \\
    uint qv = (blk + 16u + g * 32u) >> 4;                                                       \\
    uvec4 lo4 = qbank4[qv];                                                                     \\
    uvec4 hi4 = qbank4[qv + 1u];                                                                \\
    [[unroll]] for (uint t = 0u; t < 8u; ++t) {                                                 \\
        uint w = (t < 4u) ? lo4[t] : hi4[t - 4u];                                               \\
        [[unroll]] for (uint b = 0u; b < 4u; ++b) {                                             \\
            uint nib = (w >> (8u * b + sh)) & 0xFu;                                             \\
            DST[dst + c + t * 4u + b] = Q_AFFINE(nib, ds, dm);                                  \\
        }                                                                                       \\
    }                                                                                           \\
  }
"""
new="""    uint sh = sub * 4u;                                                                         \\
    uint qv = (blk + 16u + g * 32u) >> 4;                                                       \\
    uvec4 lo4 = qbank4[qv];                                                                     \\
    uvec4 hi4 = qbank4[qv + 1u];                                                                \\

        uint w = (t < 4u) ? lo4[t] : hi4[t - 4u];                                               \\

    }                                                                                           \\
  }

// `ds` arrives scaled by 2^24 or 2^20 (Q4K_SCALE), `nmask` is the halfword
// mask for this step's nibble.

#define Q4K_MASK(sub) ((sub) == 0u ? 0x000F000Fu : 0x00F000F0u)

        {                                                                                       \\
            vec2 e02 = unpackHalf2x16((w) & nmask);                                             \\
            vec2 e13 = unpackHalf2x16(((w) >> 8) & nmask);                                      \\

            DST[(at) + 1u] = float16_t(ds * e13.x - dm);                                        \\
            DST[(at) + 2u] = float16_t(ds * e02.y - dm);                                        \\
            DST[(at) + 3u] = float16_t(ds * e13.y - dm);                                        \\
        }
#else
#define Q4K_SCALE(sub) 1.0
#define Q4K_MASK(sub) 0u
#define Q4K_WORD(DST, at, w)                                                                    \\
        [[unroll]] for (uint b = 0u; b < 4u; ++b) {                                             \\
            uint nib = ((w) >> (8u * b + sh)) & 0xFu;                                           \\
            DST[(at) + b] = Q_AFFINE(nib, ds, dm);                                              \\
        }
#endif
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
# the plain body's ds/mask lines: insert the scale and the mask after `float dm`
old="""    scaleMinK4(2u * g + sub, hdr.yzw, sc, mn);                                                  \\
    float ds = dd.x * float(sc);                                                                \\
    float dm = dd.y * float(mn);                                                                \\
    uint sh = sub * 4u;                                                                         \\
    uint qv = (blk + 16u + g * 32u) >> 4;                                                       \\
"""

    float ds = dd.x * float(sc) * Q4K_SCALE(sub);                                               \\
    float dm = dd.y * float(mn);                                                                \\
    uint sh = sub * 4u;                                                                         \\
    uint nmask = Q4K_MASK(sub);                                                                 \\
    uint qv = (blk + 16u + g * 32u) >> 4;                                                       \\
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)

# 3. the pipelined unpack
old="""        scaleMinK4(2u * g + sub, hdr[n].yzw, sc, mn);                                       \\
        float ds = dd.x * float(sc);                                                        \\
        float dm = dd.y * float(mn);                                                        \\
        uint sh = sub * 4u;                                                                 \\
        [[unroll]] for (uint t = 0u; t < 8u; ++t) {                                         \\
            uint w = (t < 4u) ? lo[n][t] : hi[n][t - 4u];                                   \\
            [[unroll]] for (uint b = 0u; b < 4u; ++b) {                                     \\
                uint nib = (w >> (8u * b + sh)) & 0xFu;                                     \\
                DST[dst + t * 4u + b] = Q_AFFINE(nib, ds, dm);                              \\
            }                                                                               \\
        }                                                                                   \\
    }
"""
new="""        scaleMinK4(2u * g + sub, hdr[n].yzw, sc, mn);                                       \\
        float ds = dd.x * float(sc) * Q4K_SCALE(sub);                                       \\
        float dm = dd.y * float(mn);                                                        \\
        uint sh = sub * 4u;                                                                 \\
        uint nmask = Q4K_MASK(sub);                                                         \\
        [[unroll]] for (uint t = 0u; t < 8u; ++t) {                                         \\
            uint w = (t < 4u) ? lo[n][t] : hi[n][t - 4u];                                   \\
            Q4K_WORD(DST, dst + t * 4u, w)                                                  \\
        }                                                                                   \\
    }
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)

# 4. the kt loop
old="""#define MMA_BLOCK(K0, WME)                                                                 \\
    [[unroll]] for (uint kt = 0u; kt < BK_TILES; kt++) {                                   \\"""
new="""#define MMA_BLOCK(K0, WME)                                                                 \\
    KT_UNROLL for (uint kt = 0u; kt < BK_TILES; kt++) {                                    \\"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")

---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].
====

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

p='shaders/llm_moe_gemm.comp'
s=open(p).read()

# knob
old="""#ifndef MOE_KT_LOOP
#define MOE_KT_LOOP 0
#endif
"""
new="""#ifndef MOE_KT_LOOP
#define MOE_KT_LOOP 0
#endif
// PIPE_A=0 keeps the B pipeline and stages A plainly at the top of the step

#ifndef PIPE_A
#define PIPE_A 1
#endif
"""

old="""    uint slots = MOE_USED + 1u;
    [[unroll]] for (uint n = 0u; n < A_ITERS; ++n) {

        uint c = (idx - r * (BK / A_VEC)) * A_VEC;
        aV[n] = hact4[(pc.xnOff + (aP[n] / slots) * pc.lda + k0 + c) / A_VEC];
    }
"""
new="""    uint slots = MOE_USED + 1u;
#if PIPE_A
    [[unroll]] for (uint n = 0u; n < A_ITERS; ++n) {
        uint idx = tid + n * LANES;
        uint r = idx / (BK / A_VEC);
        uint c = (idx - r * (BK / A_VEC)) * A_VEC;
        aV[n] = hact4[(pc.xnOff + (aP[n] / slots) * pc.lda + k0 + c) / A_VEC];

#endif
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)

old="""void pipeUnpack(uint k0, uint tid, uvec4 aV[A_ITERS], uvec4 hdr[B_ITERS], uvec4 lo[B_ITERS], uvec4 hi[B_ITERS]) {
    [[unroll]] for (uint n = 0u; n < A_ITERS; ++n) {
"""
new="""void pipeUnpack(uint k0, uint tid, uvec4 aV[A_ITERS], uvec4 hdr[B_ITERS], uvec4 lo[B_ITERS], uvec4 hi[B_ITERS]) {
    if (PIPE_A != 0) [[unroll]] for (uint n = 0u; n < A_ITERS; ++n) {
"""

k=s.index("#define STAGE_A(K0)\n#endif\n", j)+len("#define STAGE_A(K0)\n#endif\n")
stage=s[j:k]
s=s[:j]+s[k:]
s=s[:i]+stage+s[i:]

new="""#if PIPE_A
#define PIPE_STAGE_A(K0)
#else
#define PIPE_STAGE_A(K0) STAGE_A(K0)
#endif
#define K_LOOP(WME)                                                                        \\
    for (uint k0 = 0u; k0 < pc.gemmK; k0 += BK) {                                          \\
        PIPE_STAGE_A(k0)                                                                   \\
        pipeUnpack(k0, tid, pA, pH, pL, pI);                                               \\"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")

68:| [§2.11](2.11-moe-gemm-pipeline.md) | The grouped MoE GEMM's K loop as a software pipeline | **The up projection 1.68x at 2048 tokens (2.01x at 512, 1.57x at 4096), bit-identical; 22 → 37 TFLOP/s executed.** The controls say the LDS round trip §2.2 blamed is ~8 points and the loop without its stagings runs at the pipe; the cost was the dependent, divergent bank-load chain in front of every K-step, each block's lines re-read two to eight times. Fetch a step ahead, a header once a super-block, a nibble group once per two steps; the register-built fragment (G5 as written) has nothing to buy |
69:| [§2.12](2.12-moe-short-tiles.md) | The grouped MoE GEMM's short last tile: the alignment one fragment, the loop one of WM copies | **`moe.down` 1.23x (1.28x on the served IQ4_NL) and `moe.up` 1.11x at 2048 tokens, bit-identical; prefill 1 417 → 1 514 tok/s at 2048 (1.07x), 1 500 → 1 549 at 4096.** The padding factor 1.90x → 1.19x (the up m4 build executes as 1.41x: any third copy of its loop spills, so it keeps the 2- and 4-tile ones); a control with the alignment forced back to 64 prices the four-copy build at −9%; the m2/m4 boundary moves from 1024 tokens to 256. The short tiles are bound by the slab unpack, ~300 VALU a lane a step at a matrix clock each |
70:| [§2.10](2.10-valu-costs-matrix-clocks.md) | Every VALU instruction costs the matrix pipe a clock; the LDS-staged GEMM's second K tile as a loop | **80 → 85% per clock, bit-identical; H3's projections 40.4 → 43.5 TFLOP/s, a 480p forward 27.3 → 26.7 s.** The register allocator's ~40 `v_swap`/`v_mov` a tile were 7% of the pipe; a probe that adds the kernel's parts back to the register-only loop prices VALU at ~3% an instruction a MMA, the LDS reads at 3%, the barrier's lockstep at 6–9, and the 16-lane exchange (`v_permlanex16`) as a loss |
114:| [P14](p14-prefill-at-depth.md) | **The gather, and 128k prefills past 900 tok/s — the target met.** A 128 000-cell prefill goes from P13's **563.6** to **826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048** (1.47x, falloff from depth zero 0.50x → 0.72x) and to **946.1 at 8192**, with decode unmoved as the control. [← IDEAS.md](ideas.md) · [research index](README.md) · the grouped MoE GEMM's unpack

### 2.13 The Q4_K nibble as an f16 denormal: the slab unpack's VALU 331 → 259 a step, bit-identical, `moe.up` 1.02x — and the move storm and the A prefetch priced as dead — **done** ✅ (2026-09-30)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G5, after §2.12): the up projection's short tiles
are bound by the slab unpack, "~300 VALU a lane a K-step, every
instruction a matrix clock" (§2.10). §2.11 left G5's argument for
`v_perm`/`v_cvt_pk` sequences over per-element work. What does the unpack
actually spend per element, and how much of it can go without moving a
bit of the slab?

**Answer: less than the estimate hoped.** Read from the ISA, an element of
the shipped unpack is three VALU instructions, not five: the compiler
already fuses the fma and the half conversion into one `v_fma_mixlo_f16`
/ `v_fma_mixhi_f16`, so what stands in front of it is a `v_bfe_u32` and a
`v_cvt_f32_u32`. Both go: **a halfword whose low nibble is the value and
whose other twelve bits are zero *is* the half `nib × 2^-24`**, an exact
denormal, and `v_fma_mix` reads a half from either half of a word for
free (op_sel). A word's four nibbles become two masked words — `w &
0x000F000F` holds elements 0 and 2, `(w >> 8) & mask` elements 1 and 3 —
three instructions for four elements instead of eight, and the scale
carries the 2^24 (2^20 for the high nibble, whose halfword is `nib ×
16`). `d × sc` is an 11-by-6-bit product, exact in fp32, and a power of
two keeps it exact, so the fma sees the same operands to the bit and the
slab is byte-identical. The full four-tile K-step's non-MMA VALU goes
**331 → 259** (of ~2 176 clocks of MMA), and `moe.up` at 2048 tokens
**6 236 / 6 298 → 6 180 / 6 115 µs (1.02x)**, 1.013x at 512, 1.02x at
1024, 1.024x at 4096. Shipped on the seven Q4_K up builds (`-DNIB_F16=1`).
Two other arms on the same step measured dead: keeping the two K tiles as
a loop (§2.10's fix) *adds* moves here (38 a tile from the allocator), and
fetching A at the top of the step instead of a step ahead removes 65 of
the 71 moves and costs **12%**, because the exposed A latency is worth
far more than the moves.

**The step, from the ISA** (`cmd/probe`, `RADV_DEBUG=asm`, the four-tile
copy of `up_q4k_m4`'s K loop, one wave64, two 64-column slabs, BK 32):

| VALU a step (64 MMAs beside it) | shipped (§2.12) | `NIB_F16` |
|---|---:|---:|
| nibble extract + int→float (`v_bfe_u32`, `v_cvt_f32_u32`) | 64 + 64 | 0 |
| nibble masks (`v_and_b32`, `v_lshrrev_b32`) | — | 48 |
| `v_fma_mixlo/hi_f16` (the floor: one an element) | 64 | 64 |
| allocator moves (`v_mov_b32`, `v_swap_b32`) | 65 | 71 |
| the scale path (`scaleMinK4`, `v_cndmask`, `v_bfe`, 4 `v_cvt`, 4 `v_fma_mix_f32`, 2 `v_mul`) | ~32 | ~34 |
| addresses and the A store | ~42 | ~42 |
| **non-MMA VALU** | **331** | **259** |

Whole shader: 2 504 → 2 401 instructions, 256 VGPRs, no spill, at every
build. The same knob on the other rungs: m1 216 VGPRs, m2 240, n2m1 144,
n1m1 96 — and **those loops carry 4–6 moves a step where the m4 carries
71**. The move storm is register pressure at 256, not the unroll.

**The arms** (`cmd/llm -moe -model <shard> -tokens 512,1024,2048,4096
-iters 60`, layer 3, the 4k trace's real routing, the checkpoint's Q5_1
down, the m4 rung at every count since §2.12's plan; each pair of
binaries interleaved twice the same minutes; 100 ms clock and package
samples, median 2 683–2 721 MHz at 145–147 W on every arm but the last,
which ran at 2 760 because its pipe was idler):

| `moe.up`, µs a layer | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| shipped (§2.12) | 2 960 / 2 964 | 4 075 / 4 118 | 6 236 / 6 298 | 10 235 / 10 205 |
| **`NIB_F16`** | **2 922 / 2 921** | **4 022 / 4 016** | **6 180 / 6 115** | **9 941 / 10 014** |
| `NIB_F16` again, the next pair's control | 2 962 / 2 927 | 4 053 / 4 030 | 6 098 / 6 119 | 9 995 / 10 361 |
| `NIB_F16` + `PIPE_A=0` (A fetched at the top of the step) | 3 290 / 3 280 | 4 546 / 4 508 | 7 014 / 6 887 | 11 225 / 11 311 |
| `MOE_KT_LOOP` (the K tiles as a loop) | not timed: 38 moves a tile in the ISA, 82 a step against 65 | | | |

The block: 6 323 / 6 332 → 6 297 / 6 297 at 512, 8 749 / 8 800 → 8 694 /
8 692 at 1024, 13 708 / 13 763 → 13 655 / 13 600 at 2048, 22 635 /
22 607 → 22 300 / 22 465 at 4096. `moe.down` does not move (it is not
this kernel's build).

**Why 2% and not the 6% the count predicts for a short tile.** 72 VALU
of ~2 500 clocks is 2.9% at a full tile and 5% at the two-tile copy the
up build executes its tails as; the measured 2% says the unpack's VALU
was only partly on the critical path — the four waves a SIMD overlap one
wave's unpack with another's MMAs some of the time, which §2.10's probe
(one kernel, VALU *between* its own MMAs) does not see. The count is the
upper bound on what a VALU cut buys here, not its price.

**What the two dead arms say about the rest of the step.** The 71 moves
are the allocator assembling eight-register fragments out of scattered
`ds_load_b64` pairs at a 256-VGPR limit; the sixteen registers of the A
prefetch are the difference between that and the m2 build's four moves,
and taking them (fetch A from the hoisted permutation entries at the top
of each step, `PIPE_A=0`) removes the moves and loses 12%: the A latency
the pipeline hides is worth ~6x the moves it costs. So the moves stay,
bounded at ~3% (71 clocks of ~2 500), and the up projection's step is
now: 64 MMAs, 64 fma_mix (the floor), ~50 mask instructions, ~70 moves
that cannot be bought, ~75 of scale path and addresses, 24 fragment
reads (~8%, §2.11) and 12 LDS stores. There is no 5% left in the unpack.

**Gates.** `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` with the new m4 loaded through
`LLM_MOE_SPV` against the embedded (old) m2/m2: `maxAbs == 0` on every
mixed plan (so RADV preserves fp16 denormals and `v_fma_mix`'s half
input conversion honours them on this part — a build that flushed would
have failed with every value `-dm`); `TestMoEGPUPaddingIsInert` passes;
the negative control (a `MOE_NIB_ONLY` build through the same override)
fails the same gate, so the override was live. With the seven builds
regenerated: the whole `TestMoEGPU*` suite passes, and `TestGraphLogits`
prints %%LOGITS%%.

**In the whole model** (`cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048,4096,8192 -ctx 8192`,
48 layers, the shipped banks under `LLM_BANK_CACHE`, old and new binaries
interleaved twice): %%GRAPH%%. The rung ladder at the plan boundary
(`-tokens 256,512 -ladder -iters 30`): %%LADDER%%.

**Refused on the way.** Packed-f16 math for the affine (`v_pk_fma_f16`,
two elements an instruction) is not bit-identical — `d × sc` rounds to
eleven bits — and the f16 magic-number forms (`0x6400 | nib` = 1024 +
nib) put a `1024 × ds` term into the constant whose rounding is larger
than the result's; `v_cvt_f32_ubyte0..3` on a masked word is one
instruction an element where the denormal is three for four; a
16-entry per-block table is a register-indexed lookup, which is a
`v_cndmask` chain. Q5_K (layer 2 of 48) and Q8_0 (the shared expert,
signed bytes: a denormal has no sign to give) keep the shipped unpack.

**Reproduce.** `-DNIB_F16=1` on the seven `llm_moe_up_q4k_*` generate
lines in `shaders/shaders.go`; `-DPIPE_A=0` and `-DMOE_KT_LOOP=1` are the
dead arms, kept as knobs. The screen is `cmd/llm -moe -model
models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf
-tokens 512,1024,2048,4096 -iters 60` with each arm through
`LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=…` (the model must be the shard: the directory
holds four checkpoints and the bench refuses to pick).
EOF

content.text:
G5d is done and recorded. Nothing else is outstanding, so here is the recap.

**What I did.** KERNELS.md's handoff named the next item as the Q4_K slab unpack's VALU in the MoE up GEMM, so I read the shipped `up_q4k_m4` ISA before building anything. The unpack costs three instructions an element, not the five the estimate assumed: the compiler already fuses the affine and the half conversion into one `v_fma_mixlo/hi_f16`, leaving only an extract and an int-to-float in front of it. Both go by reading each nibble as an f16 denormal. A halfword holding one nibble is exactly the half `nib × 2^-24`, `v_fma_mix` reads it straight from the word, and the scale carries the power of two, which keeps every product exact. The slab is byte-identical.

**Measured, shipped on the seven Q4_K up builds as `-DNIB_F16=1`:**

| | shipped | new |
|---|---:|---:|
| non-MMA VALU per four-tile K-step | 331 | 259 |
| `moe.up` at 2048 tokens, µs, two runs | 6 236 / 6 298 | 6 180 / 6 115 |
| whole-model prefill at 2048, tok/s, two runs | 1 513.1 / 1 512.7 | 1 521.1 / 1 523.3 |

The gain is 1.3 to 2.5 percent on the kernel and 0.4 to 0.6 percent on prefill, at the same clock and power. The count predicted 3 to 5 percent, so the VALU was only partly on the critical path with four waves a SIMD.

**Gates.** The ladder test with the new m4 against the embedded old m2/m2 agrees at maxAbs 0 on every mixed plan, a wrong-by-construction build through the same override fails it, the whole MoE suite passes on the regenerated builds, and the whole-model logits line reproduces to the digit against the old test binary.

**Two arms measured dead on the remaining 71 allocator moves a step.** Keeping the K tiles as a loop adds 38 moves a tile in the ISA and was not timed. Fetching A at the top of the step instead of a step ahead removes the moves but costs 12 percent to the exposed latency. Both stay as knobs. With three consecutive arms at or under 2 percent, G5 is closed on this kernel per decision 7.

**Record.** Filed as §2.13 in `research/2.13-moe-nibble-denormal.md`, with the G5 row, a G5d section, the how-to-run note and a session-8 handoff in KERNELS.md, rows in `research/README.md` and TODO.md, CSVs under `results/g5d_*`, and two memory notes updated. One trap for the record: `cmd/llm -moe` needs the shard as `-model`, since the checkpoint directory holds four GGUFs and every arm exits in a second otherwise.

**Not done.** The served binary still needs a redeploy, as before. The next stage per the plan's order is G4 (attention) or G6 (the streaming kernels).
